The count is not what protects it.\n\nD. \"Hand-ticked or carried-over findings fake a clean ledger.\" FAILS. Findings never cross SHAs (review.md:270-283), `preserve_prior` deliberately does not merge ledgers (review.sh:633-637), and gate 4 demands BOTH a clean ledger and `local-review/summary == success`, which review.sh computes from the same run (review.sh:1030-1043, pr_merge.py:180-186).\n\nE. \"Autofix races pr_merge.\" FAILS \u2014 gate 6(a) is kept (pr_merge.py:212-222) and the REST sha guard is atomic.\n\nF. \"The cap is an independent second opinion on the loop.\" FAILS, decisively and in reverse: autofix.sh:60 and pr_merge.py:236 read the SAME `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP`. Raising it raises both at once, so gate 6(b) never was an independent bound on anything.\n\nG. Coverage: the review that greenlights the head diffs the FULL `MERGE_BASE..HEAD_SHA` range (review.sh:489-494), so every fix commit's content is inside the approving review no matter how many there were. The count adds no content-coverage property.\n\nH. Reachability. results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:876: "verdict": "The skeleton is right and should not be rebuilt: gate ordering, head-SHA-bound single COMMENT review with marker idempotency, findings-as-task-list feeding a commit status, trusted-ref personas, double sanitization of the diff as untrusted data, fail-closed on an unparseable verdict, and an auditable adjudication exit. What is not satisfactory is everything about how the model is bounded \u2014 and it is one root cause with four symptoms. The reviewer is given a truncated diff (dispatch.sh caps the attachment at 20,000 bytes regardless of MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES: 2.9% of PR 7's patch, ~19% of PR 5's, and even PR 21's 25.6 KB diff was cut), no memory of prior rounds, no read scope, and no time, turn or byte budget, inside a home directory that contains 130 MB of committed agent transcripts at results/telemetry/sessions/ \u2014 which dispatch.sh keeps growing during the run. So it substitutes filesystem archaeology for diff reading: on PR 21, 326 of 656 commands never named a PR file and produced 83.8% of all tool output; 101 commands mined results/telemetry for 49.7% of the bytes; 20 commands hit the 1 MiB output cap and alone account for 73.2%; the diff was re-derived 277 times with git diff/show/log despite being attached and on disk. The single biggest issue is therefore unbounded scope, not unbounded time \u2014 the missing timeout is what lets it run 106 minutes on 188 changed lines (34 s per changed line, 246x PR 7 round 1), but the missing scope is what makes those minutes worthless. It degrades all four axes at once: precision (findings anchored to whatever it happened to read, PR 21 F10/F11 relitigating settled policy), convergence (memoryless rounds re-raise 8 of 17 on PR 7 round 4; the project's own telemetry diagnosed this on PR 0001 \u2014 \"a fresh reviewer per round has no memory of prior adjudications and unbounded depth\"), cost (34.06M input tokens for 13 findings on a workflow amendment; 217M across 26 runs), and the operator (four PR 7 rounds, 76 model-minutes, zero approvals, terminated only by hand adjudication). The fixes below are all prompt/config/protocol edits totalling roughly 120 lines and add no abstraction layer. One latent item did not earn a slot but is a two-line fix worth doing opportunistically: review.sh executes as $0 from the branch worktree under review, so a PR editing local/bin/review.sh would be reviewed by its own modified reviewer \u2014 have it refuse to run, or re-exec from $ROOT/local/bin/review.sh, after the primary-repo re-point at review.sh:57-68.",

This is the part that keeps the record honest.",

results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:895:    "why": "There is no wall-clock, turn or output bound anywhere in the review path (grep for timeout in review.sh/dispatch.sh returns nothing); MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT=1800 only bounds how long a second review queues. PR 21 has run 106 minutes on a 14-file/188-line diff, holding the per-PR lock while any queued review times out, with nothing that will ever stop it. The budget sentence matters as much as the timeout: a killed run yields no verdict, a budgeted one yields a verdict.",
results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:905:     "argument": "The proposal is refuted on its own factual premise and on three independent safety grounds. Evidence is from ~/MIPStarRE-qpbt and ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev on ghz.\n\n1) THE PREMISE IS FALSE. \"PR 21 ... with nothing that will ever stop it\" \u2014 it stopped. results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl records `reviewer-pr21-20260902-01 wall_s=6598 status=done`; the dispatch log ends with a `turn.completed` event carrying usage {input_tokens: 34,056,619, output_tokens: 152,179}; ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr21/7f5c58ba.../code.rc = 0. The run published a real review: 13 findings, two blockers, `VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED` (pr21/ledgers/pr21-7f5c58ba...md) \u2014 on a PR whose entire purpose is retiring a merge-time safety gate. F1 is a genuine TOCTOU in autofix.sh cap accounting (`:402-408` computed before the lock at `:541-543`); F2 is that `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts a body that merely starts with ADJUDICATION and contains `head=<sha>`. With `timeout 2400`, that review dies at minute 40 (~36% through), review.sh posts local-review/summary=failure, and the record's most safety-relevant ledger is never written. The proposal's own expected_effect (\"a run that would have burned 34M tokens self-terminates with a usable ledger instead of being killed empty\") inverts what actually happens: the unchanged lane self-terminated with a usable ledger; the proposal is what kills it empty.\n\n2) THE DEFAULT DESTROYS 15% OF ALL SUCCESSFUL REVIEWS EVER RUN. From sessions.jsonl, of 26 reviewer sessions with status=done, four exceed 2400 s: reviewer-pr0001-...-07 = 2657, reviewer-pr5-...-01 = 3622, reviewer-pr5-...-02 = 3609, reviewer-pr21-...-01 = 6598. PR 5 is the ONLY PR in the record that ever converged \u2014 findings 5, 4, 4, 0, ending `VERDICT: APPROVED` (pr5/b5da371.../code-last-message.md). Its rounds 1 and 2 \u2014 the two rounds that found the 5 and 4 real defects that drove the convergence \u2014 both exceed the proposed cap by ~20 minutes and would have been killed with zero output. A bound whose default deletes both productive rounds of the only converging review is not a safety net; it is a defect filter tuned to remove the expensive findings.\n\n3) IT DEADLOCKS THE MERGE GATE AND MAKES \u00a712 ADJUDICATION UNREACHABLE. pr_merge.py check_review raises `GateFailure(\"gate 4 (review): no review carrying <marker> on commit ...\")` BEFORE it ever consults the `adjudicated` flag or looks for an ADJUDICATION comment. A timeout publishes no marker-bound review at all. So a PR whose honest review exceeds the cap can be merged neither by verdict nor by operator adjudication \u2014 review.md \u00a712's only escape hatch requires a published review on that exact head. Re-running is deterministic: same diff, same corpus, same wall. The proposal converts \"slow but eventually correct\" into \"permanently unmergeable until the operator discovers and raises an undocumented env var,\" which is a worse failure mode than the stall it targets, and it silently rewrites the \u00a712 contract.\n\n4) THE BUDGET SENTENCE OPENS A FAIL-OPEN APPROVE. review.sh's parser injects a synthetic blocking finding only when the ledger is empty AND the verdict is not APPROVED (`if not entries and verdict != \"APPROVED\"`). An APPROVED trailer over `- none` yields UNRESOLVED_TOTAL=0, and review.sh:1043-1047 then sets SUMMARY_STATE=success, which gate 4 reads as clean. \"When either is spent, emit the Findings ledger and VERDICT from what you already have\" explicitly authorizes a verdict on incomplete evidence, and on a diff where nothing has surfaced in the first 120 commands the compliant output is APPROVED with an empty ledger. Nothing downstream \u2014 not the ledger, not the status, not the marker \u2014 records that the review was truncated. Today a stalled reviewer posts no status and nothing merges (fail-safe); after this change a budget-truncated reviewer can post a green status (fail-open). That is a direct precision-and-safety regression.\n\n5) THE 120-COMMAND FIGURE IS MEASURABLY BELOW WHERE THE FINDINGS COME FROM. Indexing PR 21's dispatch log by command_execution order: the first command touching .github/prompts/auto-fix-* is #119, docs/pr_review_management.md #127, gh_common.py #144, docs/CONTRIBUTING.md #171. Findings F12, F10, F9 are built on exactly those reads, and F10 is the finding that the PR's replacement of user consent with operator adjudication contradicts the pinned \"never merge without consulting the user\" rule. A 120-command budget deletes three findings including the governance one. Worse, F5 (\"the amendment cites a PR #5 telemetry incident absent from this head\") is only derivable by grepping results/telemetry \u2014 the corpus the companion measurement lane calls pure waste. Off-diff reading is not this reviewer's overhead; it is where its cross-file contract findings come from. Cutting it by clock or command count cuts precision, not fat.\n\n6) THE COST CLAIM IS BACKWARDS. Tokens bill as the turn proceeds; killing at 2400 s does not refund them. PR 5 round 1 would have burned roughly 12M of its 18.5M input tokens for zero output and then needed a full re-run \u2014 run_agent never passes --resume, so nothing is recoverable. The change can raise total spend on precisely the PRs it claims to protect. The measured lever that actually saves money without losing findings is scope, not clock: 101 of PR 21's 658 commands named results/telemetry and returned 49.7% of all tool output. An `.rgignore` for results/telemetry/sessions/ plus moving dispatch.sh's tee target out of the worktree removes ~half the cost while keeping every finding \u2014 cheaper in lines than this proposal and strictly dominant on the same objective.\n\n7) TWO MECHANICAL DEFECTS. (a) `timeout N codex ... | tee \"$CAPTURE\"` (dispatch.sh:631) bounds codex, not the pipeline: PIPESTATUS[0] is only evaluated after tee sees EOF, and codex's sandboxed `/bin/bash -lc` children inherit the stdout pipe, so a child outliving SIGTERM leaves the \"hard wall clock\" soft. It needs `timeout -k 30` at minimum. (b) The ~8 lines proposed for run_agent are dead code: review.sh:941-945 already posts `post_summary failure` and dies whenever the lane exits non-zero with an empty CODE_OUT, and a timeout-killed codex writes no `-o` file, so rc=124 already flows through that path. The proposal's own line budget is therefore mostly the kill and the prose.\n\n8) THE STATED HARM IS OVERSTATED. LOCK_DIR is `$CACHE/locks/review-$PR_NUM.lock` (review.sh:438) \u2014 per-PR. A runaway on PR 21 blocks only another review of PR 21, never the queue at large, so \"holding the per-PR lock while any queued review times out\" does not generalize.\n\nWhat survives: a runaway guard is worth having, but as a guard against a genuinely hung process, not as a latency control, and it must never be able to produce a green or a silent gap.",
results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:906:     "amendment": "Do the scope fix first, then add a guard that cannot fail open or fail stuck.\n\n(a) Ship the scope fix alone and re-measure before capping anything: add `results/telemetry/sessions/` to a `.rgignore` in the review worktree and move dispatch.sh's event-stream tee target out of the repo into $CACHE, so the reviewer stops grepping 130 MB of prior agent transcripts (49.7% of PR 21's tool output). Re-derive the wall-clock distribution from sessions.jsonl after two or three reviews; any cap chosen before this is fitted to a cost driver that is about to disappear.\n\n(b) If a guard is still wanted, set it from the observed distribution, not intuition: `timeout -k 30 ${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT:-9000}` (2.5 h). Observed completed runs are 2657 / 3609 / 3622 / 6598 s; 2400 s sits below the 85th percentile and kills 15% of successful history. 9000 s kills nothing in the record while still bounding a truly hung process. Verify the pipeline actually dies (children inherit the tee pipe) rather than assuming rc=124 arrives.\n\n(c) Make expiry reachable by the protocol. On rc=124, publish a marker-bound review on the exact head whose body is `## Findings` / `- [ ] F1 (blocker) - \u2014 reviewer exceeded the wall-clock guard at Ns; no verdict was reached` and `VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED`, alongside local-review/summary=failure. That keeps the exact-head/marker invariant intact, keeps the PR blocked, and \u2014 unlike a bare status \u2014 leaves gate 4's `if not matching` satisfied so review.md \u00a712 operator adjudication remains available. Without this, a capped PR is unmergeable by every path the protocol defines.\n\n(d) If the budget sentence is kept, it must forbid a green outcome. Replace \"emit the Findings ledger and VERDICT from what you already have\" with: \"If you exhaust your budget before finishing, emit the ledger you have, add `- [ ] F0 (blocker) - \u2014 review incomplete: budget exhausted after N commands; areas not covered: ...`, and emit `VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Never emit APPROVED or COMMENTED from an unfinished review.\" Add a matching assertion in write_review so an APPROVED trailer that carries the incompleteness marker is rejected the same way a missing trailer is. Without this clause the sentence is a licence for a truncated APPROVE that review.sh:1043-1047 turns into a success status and pr_merge.py reads as clean.\n\n(e) Do not add a command-count budget at 120. PR 21's first reads of docs/pr_review_management.md, gh_common.py and docs/CONTRIBUTING.md are commands #127, #144 and #171, and findings F9, F10, F12 depend on them. If a count is ever added, calibrate it above the observed index at which cross-file contract findings are formed (>=300 on this evidence), and treat it as a prompt for the reviewer to start converging, not as a stop.\n\n(f) Drop the \"~8 lines in run_agent\" item: review.sh:941-945 already handles a non-zero lane exit with empty output. The real net change is (b)+(c)+(d)."
results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:912:     "argument": "The diagnosis is right (there is no wall anywhere in the review path) but the prescription, at its stated default and with its stated failure handling, makes reviews worse on this repo's own recorded corpus. Six attacks, all with evidence.\n\n1. THE DEFAULT KILLS THE THREE MOST PRODUCTIVE RUNS IN THE CORPUS. results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl holds 28 reviewer sessions with wall_s = [1,365,685,895,969,1134,1160,1200,1225,1325,1382,1393,1425,1430,1445,1505,1527,1555,1760,1892,1895,2036,2106,2180,2657,3609,3622,6598]. A 2400 s wall is p86: it kills 4/28 (14.3%); 2700 kills 3/28. Every one of those four finished with status \"done\". Two of them are PR 5 rounds 1 and 2 (reviewer-pr5-20260902-01, 3622 s; -02, 3609 s), which produced the 5-finding and 4-finding ledgers (~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr5/3b394f23.../code-last-message.md and f36df43c...) that carried PR 5 down 5 -> 4 -> 4 -> 0 to the only APPROVED verdict in the whole dataset (b5da371d..., \"VERDICT: APPROVED\", 0 unchecked). Under the proposal both are SIGTERMed at 40 min, publish nothing, and post local-review/summary=failure. The change's first effect on real history is to delete the evidence that produced the project's only convergence.\n\n2. PR 21 IS NOT A RUNAWAY \u2014 IT FINISHED, AND THE PROPOSAL WOULD HAVE MADE IT UNMERGEABLE FOREVER. reviewer-pr21-20260902-01 recorded wall_s=6598, status done; code-last-message.md is 8695 B with 13 unchecked findings and \"VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED\". Now the trap: pr_merge.py check_review (local/bin/pr_merge.py:161-168) raises `if not matching` \u2014 no review carrying the marker on the head \u2014 BEFORE it ever reaches the `if not adjudicated` branch at :184. A head that never receives a published review fails gate 4 with AND without --adjudicated, and review.md section 12 requires the ADJUDICATION comment to list \"the last round's findings\", which do not exist. PR 21's length is structural (unscoped search surface), not variance, so every retry is killed at the same wall. The proposal converts \"slow review, real verdict, red status the author can act on\" into \"no verdict, no sanctioned merge path, ever\". That is strictly worse than the status quo, in which a slow review still lands a verdict.\n\n3.
